Centre of Mass.question: Two particles of masses 2 kg and 3 kg are placed at x = 0 m and x = 10 m respectively. The position of the centre of mass is:
The centre of mass of a body depends upon:
Centre of Mass.solution: Centre of mass depends on how mass is distributed in the body.

Centre of Mass.question: Two equal masses are placed at x = -4 m and x = 4 m. The centre of mass is located at:
Assertion (A): The centre of mass of a uniform rod lies at its midpoint. Reason (R): The mass is uniformly distributed throughout the rod.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation.
A is true, R is false.
A is false, R is true.
Centre of Mass.solution: For uniform distribution, centre of mass coincides with geometric centre.

Centre of Mass.question: The SI unit of centre of mass is:
Centre of Mass.solution: Centre of mass is a position coordinate measured in metres.

Centre of Mass.question: Two particles of masses 5 kg and 5 kg are placed at 2 m and 8 m. The centre of mass is:
The centre of mass of a uniform circular ring lies at:
Centre of Mass.solution: By symmetry, the centre of mass is at the geometric centre.

Centre of Mass.question: If one mass is much larger than the other, the centre of mass lies:
options: B) Closer to the heavier mass
C) Closer to the lighter mass
D) Outside the line joining them
Centre of Mass.solution: Centre of mass is pulled towards the heavier mass.

Centre of Mass.question: The centre of mass of a uniform rectangular sheet lies at:
Centre of Mass.solution: By symmetry, the centre of mass is at the geometric centre.

Centre of Mass.question: Two particles of masses 1 kg and 3 kg are placed at 0 m and 8 m. The centre of mass is:
The centre of mass of a system:
options: A) Must lie inside the body
B) Can lie outside the body
C) Always lies at the geometric centre
D) Always coincides with the centre of gravity
Centre of Mass.solution: For hollow or irregular shapes, centre of mass can lie outside the material.

Centre of Mass.question: Which of the following has its centre of mass outside the material of the object?
Centre of Mass.solution: For a circular ring, the centre of mass is at the centre where there is no material.

Centre of Mass.question: If two equal masses are placed at x = 2 m and x = 10 m, the centre of mass is:
Which quantity is required to calculate the centre of mass of two particles?
Centre of Mass.solution: Centre of mass depends on masses and their positions.

Centre of Mass.question: The formula for the centre of mass of two particles along the x-axis is:
Centre of Mass.solution: X_cm = (m₁x₁ + m₂x₂)/(m₁+m₂)

Motion of Centre of Mass.question: The motion of the centre of mass of a system depends on:
Motion of Centre of Mass.solution: Only external forces can change the motion of the centre of mass.

Motion of Centre of Mass.question: If no external force acts on a system, the centre of mass moves with:
Motion of Centre of Mass.solution: According to Newton's Second Law, F_ext = Ma_cm. If F_ext = 0, a_cm = 0. Hence, the centre of mass moves with constant velocity.

Motion of Centre of Mass.question: The acceleration of the centre of mass is given by:
Motion of Centre of Mass.solution: a_cm = F_ext/M

Motion of Centre of Mass.question: Assertion (A): Internal forces cannot change the motion of the centre of mass. Reason (R): Internal forces always occur in equal and opposite pairs.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation.
A is true, R is false.
A is false, R is true.
Motion of Centre of Mass.solution: Internal forces cancel out in pairs, so they cannot change the motion of the centre of mass.

Motion of Centre of Mass.question: A bomb explodes in mid-air into several fragments. Neglect air resistance. The centre of mass of the fragments follows:
options: C) The same parabolic path as before the explosion
Motion of Centre of Mass.solution: Since no external force acts during explosion, the centre of mass continues along the same parabolic path.

Motion of Centre of Mass.question: The SI unit of acceleration of the centre of mass is:
Motion of Centre of Mass.solution: Acceleration is measured in m/s².

Motion of Centre of Mass.question: A system of particles has a total mass of 10 kg. An external force of 20 N acts on it. The acceleration of the centre of mass is:
Which force affects the motion of the centre of mass?
options: C) Friction between particles of the system
Motion of Centre of Mass.solution: Only external forces affect the motion of the centre of mass.

Motion of Centre of Mass.question: If the net external force on a system is doubled while the mass remains constant, the acceleration of the centre of mass becomes:
Motion of Centre of Mass.solution: Since a = F/M, doubling F doubles a.

Motion of Centre of Mass.question: In the absence of external forces, the momentum of a system:
Motion of Centre of Mass.solution: Momentum is conserved when no external force acts.

Motion of Centre of Mass.question: Two ice skaters push each other apart on a frictionless surface. The centre of mass of the two-skater system:
options: A) Moves toward the heavier skater
B) Remains at rest if initially at rest
C) Moves toward the lighter skater
Motion of Centre of Mass.solution: Since no external force acts, the centre of mass remains at rest.

Motion of Centre of Mass.question: The motion of the centre of mass obeys:
Motion of Centre of Mass.solution: F_ext = Ma_cm is Newton's Second Law applied to the centre of mass.

Motion of Centre of Mass.question: A rocket moves in space by ejecting gases. The motion of the rocket is due to:
options: B) Conservation of momentum and external-force analysis of the rocket system
Motion of Centre of Mass.solution: Rocket propulsion is based on conservation of momentum.

Motion of Centre of Mass.question: Which equation is correct for the centre of mass?
Motion of Centre of Mass.solution: F_ext = Ma_cm is the equation of motion for the centre of mass.

Motion of Centre of Mass.question: The centre of mass of an isolated system always:
Motion of Centre of Mass.solution: An isolated system has no net external force, so the centre of mass has zero acceleration and moves with constant velocity.

Linear Momentum of a System of Particles.question: Linear momentum of a particle is defined as:
The SI unit of linear momentum is:
Linear Momentum of a System of Particles.solution: Momentum = mass × velocity, so unit is kg·m/s.

Linear Momentum of a System of Particles.question: If the velocity of a body is doubled while its mass remains constant, its momentum becomes:
Linear Momentum of a System of Particles.solution: p = mv. If v doubles, p doubles.

Linear Momentum of a System of Particles.question: Assertion (A): Momentum is a vector quantity. Reason (R): Momentum has both magnitude and direction.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation.
A is true, R is false.
A is false, R is true.
Linear Momentum of a System of Particles.solution: Momentum = mass × velocity. Since velocity is a vector, momentum is a vector.

Linear Momentum of a System of Particles.question: A body of mass 5 kg moves with a speed of 4 m/s. Its momentum is:
The total momentum of a system is:
Linear Momentum of a System of Particles.solution: Total momentum = vector sum of individual momenta.

Linear Momentum of a System of Particles.question: If no external force acts on a system, its total momentum:
Linear Momentum of a System of Particles.solution: Law of conservation of momentum: total momentum is conserved.

Linear Momentum of a System of Particles.question: A particle of mass 3 kg moves with velocity 6 m/s east. Its momentum is:
Momentum depends on:
Linear Momentum of a System of Particles.solution: p = mv, so it depends on both mass and velocity.

Linear Momentum of a System of Particles.question: Two particles have momenta 5 kg·m/s and 7 kg·m/s in the same direction. Their total momentum is:
A body is at rest. Its momentum is:
Which law is directly related to conservation of momentum?
Linear Momentum of a System of Particles.solution: Conservation of momentum follows from Newton's Third Law.

Linear Momentum of a System of Particles.question: The momentum of a system changes only due to:
Linear Momentum of a System of Particles.solution: Internal forces cannot change total momentum of the system.

Linear Momentum of a System of Particles.question: A body of mass 10 kg moves with velocity 3 m/s. Its momentum is:
The mathematical expression for the total momentum of two particles is:
Linear Momentum of a System of Particles.solution: Total momentum is the vector sum of individual momenta.

Vector Product (Cross Product) of Two Ve.question: The cross product of two vectors is represented by:
Vector Product (Cross Product) of Two Ve.solution: Cross product is denoted by ×.

Vector Product (Cross Product) of Two Ve.question: The magnitude of the cross product of two vectors is:
Vector Product (Cross Product) of Two Ve.solution: |A×B| = AB sinθ

Vector Product (Cross Product) of Two Ve.question: The direction of the cross product is determined by:
Vector Product (Cross Product) of Two Ve.solution: The right-hand thumb rule gives the direction of cross product.

Vector Product (Cross Product) of Two Ve.question: Assertion (A): The cross product of two parallel vectors is zero. Reason (R): The angle between parallel vectors is 0°, and sin 0° = 0.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation.
A is true, R is false.
A is false, R is true.
Vector Product (Cross Product) of Two Ve.solution: |A×B| = AB sinθ. For parallel vectors, θ = 0°, so sinθ = 0.

Vector Product (Cross Product) of Two Ve.question: The angle between two vectors is 90°. Their cross product is:
Vector Product (Cross Product) of Two Ve.solution: |A×B| = AB sin90° = AB, which is maximum.

Vector Product (Cross Product) of Two Ve.question: The cross product of two parallel vectors is:
Vector Product (Cross Product) of Two Ve.solution: For parallel vectors, θ = 0°, so |A×B| = 0.

Vector Product (Cross Product) of Two Ve.question: The cross product of two vectors gives a:
Vector Product (Cross Product) of Two Ve.solution: Cross product of two vectors is a vector.

Vector Product (Cross Product) of Two Ve.question: If two vectors are perpendicular, then:
Vector Product (Cross Product) of Two Ve.solution: For perpendicular vectors, θ = 90°, so |A×B| = AB sin90° = AB.

Vector Product (Cross Product) of Two Ve.question: The SI unit of the cross product depends upon:
options: A) The units of the vectors
Vector Product (Cross Product) of Two Ve.solution: The unit of cross product depends on the units of the vectors being multiplied.

Vector Product (Cross Product) of Two Ve.question: If either vector has zero magnitude, the cross product is:
Vector Product (Cross Product) of Two Ve.solution: If A = 0 or B = 0, then |A×B| = 0.

Vector Product (Cross Product) of Two Ve.question: Which mathematical operation is not commutative?
Vector Product (Cross Product) of Two Ve.solution: A×B = -B×A, so cross product is not commutative.

Vector Product (Cross Product) of Two Ve.question: The cross product of two vectors points:
Vector Product (Cross Product) of Two Ve.solution: The cross product is perpendicular to the plane containing both vectors.

Vector Product (Cross Product) of Two Ve.question: If the angle between two vectors is 180°, then their cross product is:
Vector Product (Cross Product) of Two Ve.solution: |A×B| = AB sin180° = 0

Vector Product (Cross Product) of Two Ve.question: Which formula correctly represents the magnitude of the cross product?
Vector Product (Cross Product) of Two Ve.solution: |A×B| = AB sinθ

Vector Product (Cross Product) of Two Ve.question: The cross product is widely used in calculating:
Vector Product (Cross Product) of Two Ve.solution: Torque τ = r×F is a cross product.

Angular Velocity and its Relation with L.question: Angular velocity is defined as:
options: A) Rate of change of displacement
B) Rate of change of angular displacement
C) Rate of change of momentum
D) Rate of change of force
Angular Velocity and its Relation with L.solution: ω = dθ/dt

Angular Velocity and its Relation with L.question: The SI unit of angular velocity is:
Angular Velocity and its Relation with L.solution: Angular velocity is measured in radians per second.

Angular Velocity and its Relation with L.question: The relation between linear velocity and angular velocity is:
Angular Velocity and its Relation with L.solution: v = rω

Angular Velocity and its Relation with L.question: Assertion (A): All particles of a rotating rigid body have the same angular velocity. Reason (R): Every point rotates through the same angle in the same time.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation.
A is true, R is false.
A is false, R is true.
Angular Velocity and its Relation with L.solution: For a rigid body, all points have the same angular velocity.

Angular Velocity and its Relation with L.question: A wheel rotates with an angular velocity of 5 rad/s. A point on its rim is 2 m from the centre. Its linear speed is:
Which quantity is the same for every point on a rigid body rotating about a fixed axis?
Angular Velocity and its Relation with L.solution: All points in a rigid body have the same angular velocity.

Angular Velocity and its Relation with L.question: If the radius is doubled while angular velocity remains constant, the linear velocity becomes:
Angular Velocity and its Relation with L.solution: v = rω. If r doubles, v doubles.

Angular Velocity and its Relation with L.question: A particle moving in a circle has:
options: A) Linear velocity directed toward the centre
B) Linear velocity tangential to the path
Angular Velocity and its Relation with L.solution: In circular motion, linear velocity is tangential to the path.

Angular Velocity and its Relation with L.question: If angular velocity is doubled and radius remains unchanged, the linear velocity becomes:
Angular Velocity and its Relation with L.solution: v = rω. If ω doubles, v doubles.

Angular Velocity and its Relation with L.question: A point is 0.5 m from the axis of rotation. If its angular velocity is 8 rad/s, its linear speed is:
Which quantity depends on the distance from the axis of rotation?
Angular Velocity and its Relation with L.solution: v = rω, so linear velocity depends on distance from axis.

Angular Velocity and its Relation with L.question: One complete revolution corresponds to an angular displacement of:
Angular Velocity and its Relation with L.solution: 1 revolution = 2π radians

Angular Velocity and its Relation with L.question: If a rotating body has zero angular velocity, then its linear velocity is:
Angular Velocity and its Relation with L.solution: v = rω. If ω = 0, then v = 0.

Angular Velocity and its Relation with L.question: Which formula correctly relates angular velocity to time period T?
Angular Velocity and its Relation with L.solution: ω = 2π/T

Angular Velocity and its Relation with L.question: Two points are located at distances 1 m and 3 m from the axis of a rotating disc. If the disc rotates with constant angular velocity, then:
options: A) Both points have the same linear velocity.
B) The point at 1 m has greater linear velocity.
C) The point at 3 m has greater linear velocity.
D) Both points have zero linear velocity.
Angular Velocity and its Relation with L.solution: v = rω. The point with larger r has larger v.

Torque and Angular Momentum.question: Torque is defined as:
options: A) Force acting on a body
B) Turning effect of a force
Torque and Angular Momentum.solution: Torque is the rotational analogue of force, representing the turning effect.

Torque and Angular Momentum.question: The SI unit of torque is:
Torque and Angular Momentum.solution: Torque = r × F, so unit is N·m.

Torque and Angular Momentum.question: The magnitude of torque is given by:
Torque and Angular Momentum.solution: τ = rF sinθ

Torque and Angular Momentum.question: Assertion (A): Torque is a vector quantity. Reason (R): Torque is the cross product of position vector and force.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation.
A is true, R is false.
A is false, R is true.
Torque and Angular Momentum.solution: τ = r×F, and cross product gives a vector.

Torque and Angular Momentum.question: A force of 10 N acts perpendicular to a rod 2 m long. The torque produced is:
Angular momentum is given by:
Torque and Angular Momentum.solution: L = Iω

Torque and Angular Momentum.question: The SI unit of angular momentum is:
Torque and Angular Momentum.solution: L = Iω, unit = kg·m²/s

Torque and Angular Momentum.question: If the net external torque acting on a system is zero, then:
Torque and Angular Momentum.solution: Law of conservation of angular momentum.

Torque and Angular Momentum.question: Torque is maximum when the angle between force and position vector is:
Torque and Angular Momentum.solution: τ = rF sinθ. Maximum when sinθ = 1, i.e., θ = 90°.

Torque and Angular Momentum.question: A force acts along the line joining the pivot and the point of application. The torque is:
Torque and Angular Momentum.solution: When force acts along the line of r, θ = 0°, so τ = 0.

Torque and Angular Momentum.question: Which quantity is conserved when no external torque acts?
Torque and Angular Momentum.solution: Angular momentum is conserved when net external torque is zero.

Torque and Angular Momentum.question: A wheel has a moment of inertia of 4 kg·m² and rotates with an angular velocity of 5 rad/s. Its angular momentum is:
Torque and Angular Momentum.solution: L = Iω = 4 × 5 = 20 kg·m²/s

Torque and Angular Momentum.question: Which formula relates torque and angular acceleration?
Torque and Angular Momentum.solution: τ = Iα is the rotational analogue of F = ma.

Torque and Angular Momentum.question: Torque is also known as:
Torque and Angular Momentum.solution: Torque is known by all these names.

Torque and Angular Momentum.question: The direction of torque is determined using:
Torque and Angular Momentum.solution: Right-hand thumb rule gives the direction of torque.

Equilibrium of a Rigid Body.question: A rigid body is said to be in equilibrium when:
options: A) It is only at rest.
B) It moves with constant acceleration.
C) The net force and net torque acting on it are zero.
D) Only the net force is zero.
Equilibrium of a Rigid Body.solution: Both translational and rotational equilibrium conditions must be satisfied.

Equilibrium of a Rigid Body.question: The first condition of equilibrium is:
Equilibrium of a Rigid Body.solution: First condition: net force must be zero.

Equilibrium of a Rigid Body.question: The second condition of equilibrium is:
Equilibrium of a Rigid Body.solution: Second condition: net torque must be zero.

Equilibrium of a Rigid Body.question: Assertion (A): A body can be in equilibrium while moving. Reason (R): A body moving with constant velocity has zero acceleration.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation.
A is true, R is false.
A is false, R is true.
Equilibrium of a Rigid Body.solution: Dynamic equilibrium occurs when net force is zero even with constant velocity.

Equilibrium of a Rigid Body.question: A body is acted upon by two equal and opposite forces along the same line. The body is:
Equilibrium of a Rigid Body.solution: Net force is zero, so translational equilibrium is achieved.

Equilibrium of a Rigid Body.question: The SI unit of torque is:
Equilibrium of a Rigid Body.solution: Torque is measured in Newton-metre.

Equilibrium of a Rigid Body.question: Which condition is necessary for rotational equilibrium?
Equilibrium of a Rigid Body.solution: Rotational equilibrium requires net torque to be zero.

Equilibrium of a Rigid Body.question: If the net force on a body is zero but the net torque is not zero, the body will:
options: C) Move with constant velocity without rotating
Equilibrium of a Rigid Body.solution: Net torque causes angular acceleration even if net force is zero.

Equilibrium of a Rigid Body.question: Which of the following can produce a torque?
options: A) A force applied through the axis of rotation
B) A force applied away from the axis
Equilibrium of a Rigid Body.solution: A force applied at a perpendicular distance from the axis produces torque.

Equilibrium of a Rigid Body.question: A body is in complete equilibrium if:
options: C) Both force and torque are zero
Equilibrium of a Rigid Body.solution: Complete equilibrium requires both ΣF = 0 and Στ = 0.

Equilibrium of a Rigid Body.question: A book resting on a table is an example of:
Equilibrium of a Rigid Body.solution: Static equilibrium: body at rest with zero net force and torque.

Equilibrium of a Rigid Body.question: A car moving with constant velocity on a straight road is an example of:
Equilibrium of a Rigid Body.solution: Dynamic equilibrium: constant velocity means net force is zero.

Equilibrium of a Rigid Body.question: Which of the following is not in equilibrium?
options: A) A hanging lamp at rest
B) A book lying on a table
C) A car moving with constant velocity on a straight road
Equilibrium of a Rigid Body.solution: A freely falling stone has acceleration g, so net force is not zero.

Equilibrium of a Rigid Body.question: The tendency of a force to rotate a body depends on:
options: A) Only the magnitude of the force
B) Only the distance from the axis
C) Both the force and the perpendicular distance from the axis
D) Only the mass of the body
Equilibrium of a Rigid Body.solution: Torque depends on both force magnitude and perpendicular distance.

Equilibrium of a Rigid Body.question: Which equations together represent the conditions for equilibrium of a rigid body?
Equilibrium of a Rigid Body.solution: Both ΣF = 0 and Στ = 0 are required for equilibrium.

Moment of Inertia.question: Moment of inertia is the rotational analogue of:
Moment of Inertia.solution: Mass resists linear motion, while moment of inertia resists rotational motion.

Moment of Inertia.question: The SI unit of moment of inertia is:
Moment of Inertia.solution: I = mr², so unit is kg·m².

Moment of Inertia.question: The moment of inertia depends upon:
options: B) Distance of mass from the axis only
C) Both mass and distribution of mass about the axis
Moment of Inertia.solution: I depends on mass and how it is distributed about the axis.

Moment of Inertia.question: Assertion (A): Moment of inertia depends on the axis of rotation. Reason (R): The distances of mass elements from the axis change with the axis.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation.
A is true, R is false.
A is false, R is true.
Moment of Inertia.solution: Different axes mean different distances, so I changes.

Moment of Inertia.question: The mathematical expression for the moment of inertia of a particle is:
Moment of Inertia.solution: I = mr²

Moment of Inertia.question: A particle of mass 2 kg is at a distance of 3 m from the axis of rotation. Its moment of inertia is:
Moment of Inertia.solution: I = mr² = 2 × 3² = 18 kg·m²

Moment of Inertia.question: If the distance of a particle from the axis is doubled, its moment of inertia becomes:
Moment of Inertia.solution: I ∝ r². If r doubles, I becomes 4 times.

Moment of Inertia.question: Which of the following has the greatest moment of inertia about its centre for the same mass and radius?
Moment of Inertia.solution: The thin ring has all its mass at the maximum distance from the axis.

Moment of Inertia.question: Which factor does not affect the moment of inertia?
Moment of Inertia.solution: Colour does not affect moment of inertia.

Moment of Inertia.question: The moment of inertia of a point mass placed on the axis of rotation is:
Moment of Inertia.solution: When r = 0, I = mr² = 0.

Moment of Inertia.question: Which statement is correct?
options: A) Moment of inertia is always constant.
B) Moment of inertia depends only on velocity.
C) Moment of inertia depends on the chosen axis.
D) Moment of inertia is independent of mass.
Moment of Inertia.solution: Moment of inertia depends on the axis of rotation chosen.

Moment of Inertia.question: A particle has a moment of inertia of 32 kg·m² and mass 2 kg. Its distance from the axis is:
The radius of gyration is defined as:
options: C) Distance at which the entire mass can be assumed concentrated without changing the moment of inertia
Moment of Inertia.solution: Radius of gyration is the effective distance where all mass can be concentrated.

Moment of Inertia.question: Which formula correctly relates moment of inertia and radius of gyration?
Moment of Inertia.solution: I = Mk²

Moment of Inertia.question: A body has mass 5 kg and radius of gyration 2 m. Its moment of inertia is:
Moment of Inertia.solution: I = Mk² = 5 × 4 = 20 kg·m²

Kinematics of Rotational Motion about a.question: Angular displacement is measured in:
Kinematics of Rotational Motion about a.solution: Angular displacement is measured in radians.

Kinematics of Rotational Motion about a.question: Angular acceleration is defined as:
options: A) Rate of change of angular displacement
B) Rate of change of angular velocity
C) Rate of change of linear velocity
D) Rate of change of momentum

Kinematics of Rotational Motion about a.question: The SI unit of angular acceleration is:
Kinematics of Rotational Motion about a.solution: Angular acceleration is measured in rad/s².

Kinematics of Rotational Motion about a.question: Assertion (A): Rotational motion equations are analogous to linear motion equations. Reason (R): Angular displacement, velocity, and acceleration correspond to displacement, velocity, and acceleration.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation.
A is true, R is false.
A is false, R is true.
Kinematics of Rotational Motion about a.solution: The analogy between linear and rotational motion is well-established.

Kinematics of Rotational Motion about a.question: Which equation relates angular velocity and angular acceleration?
Kinematics of Rotational Motion about a.solution: ω = ω₀ + αt is the rotational equivalent of v = u + at.

Kinematics of Rotational Motion about a.question: A wheel starts from rest and rotates with an angular acceleration of 4 rad/s² for 3 s. Its angular velocity becomes:
The rotational equivalent of linear displacement is:
Kinematics of Rotational Motion about a.solution: Angular displacement (θ) corresponds to linear displacement (s).

Kinematics of Rotational Motion about a.question: The rotational equivalent of linear acceleration is:
Kinematics of Rotational Motion about a.solution: Angular acceleration (α) corresponds to linear acceleration (a).

Kinematics of Rotational Motion about a.question: The angular displacement for uniformly accelerated rotational motion is:
A disc rotates with a constant angular velocity of 10 rad/s. Its angular acceleration is:
Which equation is the rotational analogue of v² = u² + 2as?
One complete revolution is equal to:
A wheel rotates through 20 radians in 4 seconds with constant angular velocity. Its angular velocity is:
Which quantity remains constant during uniform rotational motion?
Kinematics of Rotational Motion about a.solution: Uniform rotational motion means constant angular velocity.

Kinematics of Rotational Motion about a.question: The rotational equation θ = ω₀t + 1/2 αt² is applicable when:
Kinematics of Rotational Motion about a.solution: It applies for constant angular acceleration.

Dynamics of Rotational Motion about a Fi.question: The rotational analogue of Newton's Second Law is:
Dynamics of Rotational Motion about a Fi.solution: τ = Iα

Dynamics of Rotational Motion about a Fi.question: Torque is directly proportional to:
Dynamics of Rotational Motion about a Fi.solution: τ = Iα, so torque is proportional to angular acceleration.

Dynamics of Rotational Motion about a Fi.question: The SI unit of angular acceleration is:
Dynamics of Rotational Motion about a Fi.solution: Angular acceleration is measured in rad/s².

Dynamics of Rotational Motion about a Fi.question: Assertion (A): A larger torque produces a larger angular acceleration for the same body. Reason (R): Moment of inertia remains constant for the same axis of rotation.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation.
A is true, R is false.
A is false, R is true.
Dynamics of Rotational Motion about a Fi.solution: α = τ/I. For constant I, larger τ means larger α.

Dynamics of Rotational Motion about a Fi.question: A body has a moment of inertia of 5 kg·m². If a torque of 20 N·m acts on it, its angular acceleration is:
Dynamics of Rotational Motion about a Fi.solution: α = τ/I = 20/5 = 4 rad/s²

Dynamics of Rotational Motion about a Fi.question: If the applied torque is zero, the angular acceleration is:
Dynamics of Rotational Motion about a Fi.solution: α = τ/I = 0 when τ = 0.

Dynamics of Rotational Motion about a Fi.question: The rotational equivalent of mass is:
Dynamics of Rotational Motion about a Fi.solution: Moment of inertia is the rotational equivalent of mass.

Dynamics of Rotational Motion about a Fi.question: A larger moment of inertia means:
options: B) Greater resistance to rotational motion
Dynamics of Rotational Motion about a Fi.solution: Larger I means more resistance to changes in rotational motion.

Dynamics of Rotational Motion about a Fi.question: If the same torque acts on two bodies, the body with the smaller moment of inertia will have:
Dynamics of Rotational Motion about a Fi.solution: α = τ/I. Smaller I means larger α.

Dynamics of Rotational Motion about a Fi.question: Which quantity causes rotational motion?
Dynamics of Rotational Motion about a Fi.solution: Torque causes rotational motion.

Dynamics of Rotational Motion about a Fi.question: The rotational equivalent of linear acceleration is:
Dynamics of Rotational Motion about a Fi.solution: Angular acceleration corresponds to linear acceleration.

Dynamics of Rotational Motion about a Fi.question: A wheel has a moment of inertia of 8 kg·m². A torque of 16 N·m acts on it. The angular acceleration is:
Dynamics of Rotational Motion about a Fi.solution: α = τ/I = 16/8 = 2 rad/s²

Dynamics of Rotational Motion about a Fi.question: Which equation correctly represents rotational dynamics?
Dynamics of Rotational Motion about a Fi.solution: τ = Iα

Dynamics of Rotational Motion about a Fi.question: A body rotates with constant angular velocity. The net torque acting on it is:
Dynamics of Rotational Motion about a Fi.solution: Constant ω means α = 0, so τ = 0.

Dynamics of Rotational Motion about a Fi.question: Which statement is correct?
options: A) Torque always changes angular velocity.
B) Torque is the rotational equivalent of force.
C) Angular acceleration exists without torque.
D) Moment of inertia is independent of mass.
Dynamics of Rotational Motion about a Fi.solution: Torque is indeed the rotational equivalent of force.

Angular Momentum in Rotation about a Fix.question: Angular momentum of a rigid body rotating about a fixed axis is given by:
Angular Momentum in Rotation about a Fix.solution: L = Iω

Angular Momentum in Rotation about a Fix.question: The SI unit of angular momentum is:
Angular Momentum in Rotation about a Fix.solution: L = Iω, unit = kg·m²/s

Angular Momentum in Rotation about a Fix.question: Angular momentum depends upon:
options: C) Moment of inertia and angular velocity
Angular Momentum in Rotation about a Fix.solution: L = Iω, so it depends on both I and ω.

Angular Momentum in Rotation about a Fix.question: Assertion (A): If no external torque acts on a system, its angular momentum remains constant. Reason (R): External torque is responsible for changing angular momentum.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation.
A is true, R is false.
A is false, R is true.
Angular Momentum in Rotation about a Fix.solution: Conservation of angular momentum follows from τ = dL/dt.

Angular Momentum in Rotation about a Fix.question: A wheel has a moment of inertia of 5 kg·m² and rotates with an angular velocity of 4 rad/s. Its angular momentum is:
Angular Momentum in Rotation about a Fix.solution: L = Iω = 5 × 4 = 20 kg·m²/s

Angular Momentum in Rotation about a Fix.question: If the angular velocity of a rotating body is doubled while its moment of inertia remains constant, its angular momentum becomes:
Angular Momentum in Rotation about a Fix.solution: L = Iω. If ω doubles, L doubles.

Angular Momentum in Rotation about a Fix.question: If the moment of inertia is doubled while angular velocity remains constant, angular momentum becomes:
Angular Momentum in Rotation about a Fix.solution: L = Iω. If I doubles, L doubles.

Angular Momentum in Rotation about a Fix.question: The direction of angular momentum is determined by:
Angular Momentum in Rotation about a Fix.solution: Right-hand thumb rule gives the direction of angular momentum.

Angular Momentum in Rotation about a Fix.question: Conservation of angular momentum occurs when:
options: A) Net external force is zero
B) Net external torque is zero
Angular Momentum in Rotation about a Fix.solution: Angular momentum is conserved when net external torque is zero.

Angular Momentum in Rotation about a Fix.question: A spinning skater pulls in her arms. Her moment of inertia decreases. According to conservation of angular momentum, her angular velocity:
Angular Momentum in Rotation about a Fix.solution: L = Iω constant. If I decreases, ω increases.

Angular Momentum in Rotation about a Fix.question: Which quantity remains constant for an isolated rotating system?
Angular Momentum in Rotation about a Fix.solution: Angular momentum is conserved in an isolated system.

Angular Momentum in Rotation about a Fix.question: A body has angular momentum 24 kg·m²/s and moment of inertia 6 kg·m². Its angular velocity is:
Angular Momentum in Rotation about a Fix.solution: ω = L/I = 24/6 = 4 rad/s

Angular Momentum in Rotation about a Fix.question: Which of the following is an application of conservation of angular momentum?
options: B) A diver tucking in while diving
Angular Momentum in Rotation about a Fix.solution: A diver reduces moment of inertia to increase angular velocity.

Angular Momentum in Rotation about a Fix.question: If the net external torque on a rotating body is positive, then its angular momentum:
Angular Momentum in Rotation about a Fix.solution: τ = dL/dt. Positive τ means L increases.

Angular Momentum in Rotation about a Fix.question: Which equation correctly relates torque and angular momentum?
Angular Momentum in Rotation about a Fix.solution: τ = dL/dt

Centre of Mass.question: Two particles of masses 3 kg and 5 kg are placed at x = 2 m and x = 8 m respectively. The centre of mass is:
Three particles of masses 1 kg, 2 kg, and 3 kg are placed at x = 0 m, 2 m, and 6 m respectively. The centre of mass is:
Assertion (A): The centre of mass of a hollow sphere is at its centre. Reason (R): The mass is symmetrically distributed about the centre.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation.
Both are true but R is not the correct explanation.
A is true, R is false.
A is false, R is true.
Centre of Mass.solution: Due to symmetry, the centre of mass of a hollow sphere is at its geometric centre.

Centre of Mass.question: Two particles have masses in the ratio 2 : 5. The centre of mass divides the distance between them in the ratio:
Centre of Mass.solution: The centre of mass divides the line joining two masses inversely proportional to their masses.

Centre of Mass.question: The centre of mass of a semicircular wire lies:
options: A) At the centre of the circle
B) Outside the wire on the axis of symmetry
C) At the end of the diameter
D) At the midpoint of the arc
Centre of Mass.solution: Centre of mass of semicircular wire lies on the axis of symmetry outside the wire at distance 2R/π from the centre.

Centre of Mass.question: A 2 kg mass is at x = 1 m, and a 6 kg mass is at x = 5 m. The centre of mass is:
If all particles of a system are shifted by 4 m along the positive x-axis, the centre of mass:
Centre of Mass.solution: Centre of mass shifts by the same amount as all particles.

Centre of Mass.question: Which statement is correct?
options: A) The centre of mass always lies inside the object.
B) The centre of mass always lies on the surface.
C) The centre of mass depends on mass distribution.
D) The centre of mass depends only on volume.
Centre of Mass.solution: Centre of mass depends on how mass is distributed in the body.

Centre of Mass.question: The centre of mass of a uniform triangular lamina is located:
options: A) At the midpoint of one side
Centre of Mass.solution: The centroid is the point of intersection of medians, which is the centre of mass.

Centre of Mass.question: A body is divided into two equal masses. The centre of mass:
options: A) Must lie midway between them
C) Must lie inside one mass
Centre of Mass.solution: Centre of mass depends on the positions of the masses.

Centre of Mass.question: The x-coordinate of the centre of mass of two particles is 4 m. One particle is 2 kg at 2 m, the other has mass 4 kg. Its position is:
If equal masses are placed at the four corners of a square, the centre of mass lies:
options: B) At the midpoint of one side
C) At the centre of the square
Centre of Mass.solution: By symmetry, the centre of mass is at the centre of the square.

Centre of Mass.question: Which factor does not affect the centre of mass?
Centre of Mass.solution: Colour does not affect the centre of mass.

Centre of Mass.question: A uniform rod is broken into two unequal pieces. The centre of mass of the combined system:
options: B) Remains unchanged (if positions are unchanged)
C) Moves to the heavier piece
Centre of Mass.solution: The centre of mass of the complete system remains the same if no external rearrangement occurs.

Centre of Mass.question: Which expression gives the x-coordinate of the centre of mass of a system of particles?
Centre of Mass.solution: x_cm = (∑m_i x_i)/(∑m_i)

Motion of Centre of Mass.question: A system of total mass 10 kg is acted upon by an external force of 50 N. The acceleration of its centre of mass is:
Assertion (A): Internal forces cannot change the velocity of the centre of mass. Reason (R): The vector sum of all internal forces is zero.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation.
A is true, R is false.
A is false, R is true.
Motion of Centre of Mass.solution: Internal forces cancel out in pairs, so they cannot change the motion of the centre of mass.

Motion of Centre of Mass.question: A bomb moving horizontally explodes into two fragments. Neglect air resistance. The centre of mass of the fragments will:
options: C) Continue along the original projectile path
D) Move in a circular path
Motion of Centre of Mass.solution: Since no external force acts during explosion, the centre of mass continues along the original path.

Motion of Centre of Mass.question: A system consists of three particles. If the net external force is zero, then the centre of mass:
options: A) Must remain at the origin
Motion of Centre of Mass.solution: F_ext = Ma_cm. If F_ext = 0, a_cm = 0, so velocity is constant.

Motion of Centre of Mass.question: A 20 kg object is split into two pieces of 5 kg and 15 kg. During the explosion, the centre of mass:
options: A) Moves toward the heavier piece
B) Changes its velocity due to internal forces
C) Continues according to the external forces only
Motion of Centre of Mass.solution: Internal forces cannot change the motion of the centre of mass.

Motion of Centre of Mass.question: The equation governing the motion of the centre of mass is:
Motion of Centre of Mass.solution: F_ext = Ma_cm

Motion of Centre of Mass.question: A system initially at rest explodes into three fragments. The vector sum of the momenta of all fragments immediately after the explosion is:
Motion of Centre of Mass.solution: By conservation of momentum, total momentum remains zero.

Motion of Centre of Mass.question: If an external force on a system is doubled while its mass is halved, the acceleration of the centre of mass becomes:
Motion of Centre of Mass.solution: a = F/M. If F doubles and M halves, a becomes 4 times.

Motion of Centre of Mass.question: A rocket moves in outer space where external forces are negligible. Which quantity remains constant for the rocket–exhaust gas system?
options: B) Momentum of the complete system
Motion of Centre of Mass.solution: Momentum of the complete system is conserved.

Motion of Centre of Mass.question: A body breaks into two unequal masses while moving. Which statement is correct?
options: A) The heavier fragment always moves faster.
B) The lighter fragment always has greater momentum.
C) The motion of the centre of mass is unaffected by the internal explosion.
D) Both fragments move in the same direction with equal speeds.
Motion of Centre of Mass.solution: Internal forces cannot change the motion of the centre of mass.

Motion of Centre of Mass.question: A 15 kg system experiences a net external force of 45 N for 4 s. The change in velocity of its centre of mass is:
Which quantity is unaffected by internal interactions within a system?
options: C) Motion of the centre of mass
Motion of Centre of Mass.solution: Internal interactions cannot affect the motion of the centre of mass.

Motion of Centre of Mass.question: During a collision of two bodies on a frictionless surface, the centre of mass:
options: C) Remains fixed at the collision point
Motion of Centre of Mass.solution: No external force acts, so the centre of mass moves with constant velocity.

Motion of Centre of Mass.question: A system is subjected to a varying external force. The acceleration of the centre of mass:
options: A) Depends only on the internal forces
B) Depends only on the external force and total mass
Motion of Centre of Mass.solution: a_cm = F_ext/M, independent of internal forces.

Motion of Centre of Mass.question: Which statement best describes the motion of the centre of mass?
options: A) It is determined by the internal arrangement of particles.
B) It depends only on the resultant external force acting on the system.
C) It always coincides with the heaviest particle.
D) It is independent of Newton's laws.
Motion of Centre of Mass.solution: The motion of the centre of mass depends only on external forces.

Linear Momentum of a System of Particles.question: Two particles of masses 2 kg and 4 kg move with velocities 3 m/s and 5 m/s in the same direction. The total momentum of the system is:
Assertion (A): In an isolated system, total linear momentum remains constant. Reason (R): No external force acts on the system.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation.
A is true, R is false.
A is false, R is true.
Linear Momentum of a System of Particles.solution: Law of conservation of momentum applies to isolated systems.

Linear Momentum of a System of Particles.question: Two bodies of masses 3 kg and 2 kg move in opposite directions with speeds 4 m/s and 5 m/s, respectively. Taking the direction of the first body as positive, the total momentum is:
A force of 15 N acts on a body for 4 s. The change in momentum is:
If the net external force on a system is zero, the momentum of the system:
Linear Momentum of a System of Particles.solution: Momentum is conserved when net external force is zero.

Linear Momentum of a System of Particles.question: Which relation correctly connects force and momentum?
A body of mass 4 kg changes its velocity from 2 m/s to 8 m/s. The change in momentum is:
During a collision between two bodies on a frictionless surface:
options: B) Kinetic energy is always conserved.
C) Both bodies stop after collision.
Linear Momentum of a System of Particles.solution: Momentum is always conserved in collisions in an isolated system.

Linear Momentum of a System of Particles.question: A 5 kg object moving at 6 m/s collides with a wall and rebounds with the same speed. The magnitude of the change in momentum is:
Which statement is correct regarding internal forces?
options: A) They change the total momentum of an isolated system.
B) They cannot change the total momentum of an isolated system.
Linear Momentum of a System of Particles.solution: Internal forces cannot change the total momentum of an isolated system.

Linear Momentum of a System of Particles.question: A system has a total momentum of 40 kg·m/s. If no external force acts, after 5 s the momentum becomes:
Linear Momentum of a System of Particles.solution: Momentum is conserved, so it remains 40 kg·m/s.

Linear Momentum of a System of Particles.question: Two particles move with equal momenta in opposite directions. The total momentum of the system is:
options: A) Equal to the momentum of either particle
B) Twice the momentum of one particle

Linear Momentum of a System of Particles.question: A 2 kg body experiences a constant force of 10 N for 3 s. The change in momentum is:
Which physical quantity is equal to impulse?
Two particles of masses 1 kg and 3 kg move with velocities 4 m/s east and 2 m/s east, respectively. The total momentum is:

Vector Product (Cross Product) of Two Ve.question: Two vectors have magnitudes 4 and 6 with an angle of 30° between them. The magnitude of their cross product is:
Assertion (A): The cross product of two vectors is zero if the vectors are parallel. Reason (R): The sine of the angle between parallel vectors is zero.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation.
A is true, R is false.
A is false, R is true.
Vector Product (Cross Product) of Two Ve.solution: |A×B| = AB sinθ. For parallel vectors, θ = 0°, so sinθ = 0.

Vector Product (Cross Product) of Two Ve.question: If A⃗ = 3î and B⃗ = 5ĵ, then A⃗×B⃗ is:
Which of the following is correct?
Vector Product (Cross Product) of Two Ve.solution: Cross product is anti-commutative: A×B = -B×A

Vector Product (Cross Product) of Two Ve.question: Two vectors have magnitudes 8 and 5. Their cross product has magnitude 20. The angle between them is:
Which unit vector is obtained from ĵ×k̂?
Which expression is always perpendicular to both vectors?
Vector Product (Cross Product) of Two Ve.solution: The cross product is perpendicular to both vectors.

Vector Product (Cross Product) of Two Ve.question: If A⃗×B⃗ = 0, then the vectors are:
Vector Product (Cross Product) of Two Ve.solution: |A×B| = AB sinθ = 0 ⇒ θ = 0° or 180°, so vectors are parallel or anti-parallel.

Vector Product (Cross Product) of Two Ve.question: The magnitude of k̂×î is:
A force of 20 N acts at 60° to a position vector of 2 m. The torque produced is:
Which of the following is not possible for a cross product?
Vector Product (Cross Product) of Two Ve.solution: Magnitude of cross product is always non-negative.

Vector Product (Cross Product) of Two Ve.question: If A⃗×B⃗ has maximum magnitude, then the angle between the vectors is:
Vector Product (Cross Product) of Two Ve.solution: |A×B| = AB sinθ. Maximum when sinθ = 1, i.e., θ = 90°.

Vector Product (Cross Product) of Two Ve.question: Which identity is correct?
Vector Product (Cross Product) of Two Ve.solution: î×î = 0 (cross product of a vector with itself is zero)

Vector Product (Cross Product) of Two Ve.question: The direction of r⃗×F⃗ represents:
Vector Product (Cross Product) of Two Ve.solution: τ = r×F, so the direction represents torque.

Vector Product (Cross Product) of Two Ve.question: Which statement about the cross product is correct?
options: A) It produces a scalar quantity.
B) It follows the commutative law.
C) It is zero when the vectors are parallel.
D) Its magnitude is AB cosθ.
Vector Product (Cross Product) of Two Ve.solution: Cross product is zero for parallel vectors.

Angular Velocity and its Relation with L.question: A wheel rotates with an angular velocity of 15 rad/s. A point on the rim is 0.4 m from the centre. Its linear velocity is:
Assertion (A): All points on a rotating rigid body have the same angular velocity. Reason (R): Every point completes one revolution in the same time.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation.
A is true, R is false.
A is false, R is true.
Angular Velocity and its Relation with L.solution: For a rigid body, all points have the same angular velocity.

Angular Velocity and its Relation with L.question: A point on a rotating disc is 3 m from the centre. If the angular velocity is 8 rad/s, its linear velocity is:
Two particles are located at distances 2 m and 5 m from the axis of a rotating disc. If the disc rotates with constant angular velocity, then:
options: A) Both have the same linear velocity.
B) The particle at 2 m has greater linear velocity.
C) The particle at 5 m has greater linear velocity.
D) Both have zero linear velocity.
Angular Velocity and its Relation with L.solution: v = rω. The particle with larger r has greater v.

Angular Velocity and its Relation with L.question: A wheel completes 300 revolutions per minute. Its angular velocity is approximately:
The relationship between angular velocity and frequency is:
Angular Velocity and its Relation with L.solution: ω = 2πf

Angular Velocity and its Relation with L.question: A wheel rotates at a constant angular velocity. Which quantity changes from point to point?
Angular Velocity and its Relation with L.solution: Linear velocity depends on distance from axis, so it changes from point to point.

Angular Velocity and its Relation with L.question: If both the radius and angular velocity are doubled, the linear velocity becomes:
Angular Velocity and its Relation with L.solution: v = rω. If r doubles and ω doubles, v becomes 4 times.

Angular Velocity and its Relation with L.question: A point moves with linear speed 12 m/s on a circular path of radius 2 m. The angular velocity is:
Angular Velocity and its Relation with L.solution: ω = v/r = 12/2 = 6 rad/s

Angular Velocity and its Relation with L.question: The period of rotation of a wheel is 0.5 s. Its angular velocity is:
Angular Velocity and its Relation with L.solution: ω = 2π/T = 2π/0.5 = 4π rad/s

Angular Velocity and its Relation with L.question: Which quantity remains the same for all particles of a rigid body in pure rotational motion?
Angular Velocity and its Relation with L.solution: All points in a rigid body have the same angular velocity.

Angular Velocity and its Relation with L.question: A point at the centre of a rotating disc has:
Angular Velocity and its Relation with L.solution: At the centre, r = 0, so v = rω = 0.

Angular Velocity and its Relation with L.question: A wheel rotates at 120 rpm. The frequency of rotation is:
If the angular velocity of a rotating body is tripled while the radius remains constant, the centripetal acceleration becomes:
Angular Velocity and its Relation with L.solution: a_c = rω². If ω triples, a_c becomes 9 times.

Angular Velocity and its Relation with L.question: Which equation correctly relates linear speed, angular velocity, and radius?
Angular Velocity and its Relation with L.solution: v = rω

Equilibrium of a Rigid Body.question: A rigid body is in equilibrium if:
options: A) Only the net force is zero.
B) Only the net torque is zero.
C) Both the net force and the net torque are zero.
D) The body is at rest only.
Equilibrium of a Rigid Body.solution: Both translational and rotational equilibrium conditions must be satisfied.

Equilibrium of a Rigid Body.question: Assertion (A): A body can have zero net force but still rotate. Reason (R): A non-zero net torque may act even when the resultant force is zero.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation.
A is true, R is false.
A is false, R is true.
Equilibrium of a Rigid Body.solution: A couple produces zero net force but non-zero torque.

Equilibrium of a Rigid Body.question: Which condition is necessary for translational equilibrium?
Equilibrium of a Rigid Body.solution: Translational equilibrium requires net force to be zero.

Equilibrium of a Rigid Body.question: Which condition is necessary for rotational equilibrium?
Equilibrium of a Rigid Body.solution: Rotational equilibrium requires net torque to be zero.

Equilibrium of a Rigid Body.question: A uniform rod of length 4 m is supported at its centre. A 20 N force acts downward at one end. What upward force must act at the other end to maintain equilibrium?
Equilibrium of a Rigid Body.solution: For equilibrium, forces must balance: F_up = 20 N

Equilibrium of a Rigid Body.question: A body is in rotational equilibrium when:
Equilibrium of a Rigid Body.solution: Rotational equilibrium means α = 0.

Equilibrium of a Rigid Body.question: Two equal and opposite forces acting along the same line produce:
Equilibrium of a Rigid Body.solution: Net force is zero and net torque is zero, so body is in equilibrium.

Equilibrium of a Rigid Body.question: Two equal and opposite parallel forces separated by a distance form a:
Equilibrium of a Rigid Body.solution: A couple consists of two equal and opposite parallel forces.

Equilibrium of a Rigid Body.question: The moment of a couple is:
Equilibrium of a Rigid Body.solution: Moment of couple = F × d (perpendicular distance)

Equilibrium of a Rigid Body.question: A couple produces:
Equilibrium of a Rigid Body.solution: A couple has zero resultant force but non-zero torque, so it produces rotation only.

Equilibrium of a Rigid Body.question: A beam is balanced on a pivot. A 30 N force acts 2 m to the left. What force at 3 m to the right keeps it in equilibrium?
Which of the following is not a condition for complete equilibrium?
Equilibrium of a Rigid Body.solution: Complete equilibrium requires ΣF = 0 and Στ = 0, not ΣL = 0.

Equilibrium of a Rigid Body.question: A body rotates with constant angular velocity about a fixed axis. It is in:
options: C) Both translational and rotational equilibrium
Equilibrium of a Rigid Body.solution: Constant angular velocity means α = 0, so it is in rotational equilibrium.

Equilibrium of a Rigid Body.question: A uniform metre scale is balanced at the 50 cm mark. A 2 kg mass is hung at the 20 cm mark. At which mark should a 1 kg mass be hung to restore equilibrium?
Which statement is correct?
options: A) Zero net force always means complete equilibrium.
B) Zero net torque always means complete equilibrium.
C) Complete equilibrium requires both zero net force and zero net torque.
D) A couple cannot rotate a body.
Equilibrium of a Rigid Body.solution: Complete equilibrium requires both ΣF = 0 and Στ = 0.

Moment of Inertia.question: The moment of inertia of a body depends upon:
options: C) Mass and distribution of mass about the axis
Moment of Inertia.solution: I depends on mass and its distribution about the axis.

Moment of Inertia.question: Assertion (A): A ring has a greater moment of inertia than a disc of the same mass and radius. Reason (R): In a ring, the entire mass is farther from the axis of rotation.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation.
A is true, R is false.
A is false, R is true.
Moment of Inertia.solution: Ring: I = MR², Disc: I = 1/2 MR². Ring has larger I.

Moment of Inertia.question: The SI unit of moment of inertia is:
Moment of Inertia.solution: I = mr², unit = kg·m²

Moment of Inertia.question: The moment of inertia of a particle of mass 5 kg situated 3 m from the axis of rotation is:
Moment of Inertia.solution: I = mr² = 5×9 = 45 kg·m²

Moment of Inertia.question: If the distance of a particle from the axis is doubled, its moment of inertia becomes:
Moment of Inertia.solution: I ∝ r². If r doubles, I becomes 4 times.

Moment of Inertia.question: Which of the following has the largest moment of inertia about its central axis (same mass and radius)?
Moment of Inertia.solution: Thin ring: I = MR² (largest), Solid disc: I = 1/2 MR², Solid sphere: I = 2/5 MR²

Moment of Inertia.question: The moment of inertia of a thin ring about its central axis is:
Moment of Inertia.solution: I_ring = MR²

Moment of Inertia.question: The moment of inertia of a solid disc about its central axis is:
Moment of Inertia.solution: I_disc = 1/2 MR²

Moment of Inertia.question: A body has a moment of inertia of 12 kg·m². If its angular acceleration is 5 rad/s², the torque acting on it is:
Which statement is correct?
options: A) Moment of inertia is a scalar quantity.
B) Moment of inertia is a vector quantity.
C) Moment of inertia depends on angular velocity.
D) Moment of inertia is independent of the axis.
Moment of Inertia.solution: Moment of inertia is a scalar quantity.

Moment of Inertia.question: The radius of gyration k is related to the moment of inertia by:
Moment of Inertia.solution: I = Mk²

Moment of Inertia.question: A body has mass 8 kg and radius of gyration 0.5 m. Its moment of inertia is:
Moment of Inertia.solution: I = Mk² = 8×0.25 = 2 kg·m²

Moment of Inertia.question: The rotational analogue of mass is:
Moment of Inertia.solution: Moment of inertia is the rotational analogue of mass.

Moment of Inertia.question: Two bodies have the same mass but different shapes. Their moments of inertia about the same type of axis are:
options: C) May be different due to mass distribution
Moment of Inertia.solution: Moment of inertia depends on mass distribution, so different shapes give different I.

Moment of Inertia.question: Which of the following standard formulas is correct?
Moment of Inertia.solution: I_rod, centre = 1/12 ML²

Kinematics of Rotational Motion about a.question: A wheel starts from rest and rotates with an angular acceleration of 4 rad/s² for 5 s. Its final angular velocity is:

Assertion (A): The equations of rotational motion are analogous to the equations of linear motion. Reason (R): Angular displacement, angular velocity, and angular acceleration correspond to displacement, velocity, and acceleration respectively.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation.
A is true, R is false.
A is false, R is true.
Kinematics of Rotational Motion about a.solution: The analogy between linear and rotational motion is well-established.

Kinematics of Rotational Motion about a.question: A rotating disc has an initial angular velocity of 10 rad/s and an angular acceleration of 3 rad/s². Find its angular velocity after 4 s.
Which equation relates angular displacement with angular velocity and angular acceleration?
Kinematics of Rotational Motion about a.solution: Both equations are valid for uniformly accelerated rotational motion.

Kinematics of Rotational Motion about a.question: A wheel rotates through 80 rad in 8 s with uniform angular velocity. The angular velocity is:
A body starts from rest with angular acceleration 2 rad/s². Angular displacement after 6 s is:
Which quantity is measured in rad/s²?
Kinematics of Rotational Motion about a.solution: Angular acceleration is measured in rad/s².

Kinematics of Rotational Motion about a.question: A wheel has an initial angular velocity of 30 rad/s and comes to rest in 10 s. The angular acceleration is:
The rotational analogue of the equation v² = u² + 2as is:
A rotating body completes 10 revolutions. Its angular displacement is:
A flywheel rotates with constant angular velocity. Its angular acceleration is:
A wheel rotates from 5 rad/s to 25 rad/s while covering 150 rad. The angular acceleration is:
Which quantity is analogous to displacement in rotational motion?
Kinematics of Rotational Motion about a.solution: Angular displacement (θ) corresponds to linear displacement (s).

Kinematics of Rotational Motion about a.question: A disc rotates with an angular acceleration of 6 rad/s² for 5 s. If its initial angular velocity is 4 rad/s, then its angular displacement is:
Which equation is valid only for constant angular acceleration?
Kinematics of Rotational Motion about a.solution: ω = ω₀ + αt is valid only for constant angular acceleration.

Dynamics of Rotational Motion about a Fi.question: A torque of 24 N·m acts on a body having a moment of inertia of 6 kg·m². The angular acceleration is:
Dynamics of Rotational Motion about a Fi.solution: α = τ/I = 24/6 = 4 rad/s²

Dynamics of Rotational Motion about a Fi.question: Assertion (A): Torque is the rotational analogue of force. Reason (R): Torque produces angular acceleration in a rotating body.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation.
A is true, R is false.
A is false, R is true.
Dynamics of Rotational Motion about a Fi.solution: Just as force produces linear acceleration, torque produces angular acceleration.

Dynamics of Rotational Motion about a Fi.question: The rotational form of Newton's Second Law is:
Dynamics of Rotational Motion about a Fi.solution: τ = Iα

Dynamics of Rotational Motion about a Fi.question: A wheel has a moment of inertia of 10 kg·m². A torque of 50 N·m acts on it. Its angular acceleration is:
Dynamics of Rotational Motion about a Fi.solution: α = τ/I = 50/10 = 5 rad/s²

Dynamics of Rotational Motion about a Fi.question: If the applied torque is doubled while the moment of inertia remains constant, the angular acceleration becomes:
Dynamics of Rotational Motion about a Fi.solution: α = τ/I. If τ doubles, α doubles.

Dynamics of Rotational Motion about a Fi.question: If the moment of inertia is doubled while the applied torque remains constant, the angular acceleration becomes:
Dynamics of Rotational Motion about a Fi.solution: α = τ/I. If I doubles, α becomes half.

Dynamics of Rotational Motion about a Fi.question: A torque of 15 N·m acts on a disc for 4 s. If its moment of inertia is 5 kg·m², the increase in angular velocity is:
Dynamics of Rotational Motion about a Fi.solution: α = 15/5 = 3 rad/s²; Δω = α×t = 3×4 = 12 rad/s

Dynamics of Rotational Motion about a Fi.question: Which quantity is analogous to mass in rotational motion?
Dynamics of Rotational Motion about a Fi.solution: Moment of inertia is the rotational analogue of mass.

Dynamics of Rotational Motion about a Fi.question: A body rotates with constant angular velocity. The net torque acting on it is:
Dynamics of Rotational Motion about a Fi.solution: Constant ω means α = 0, so τ = 0.

Dynamics of Rotational Motion about a Fi.question: The SI unit of torque is:
Dynamics of Rotational Motion about a Fi.solution: Torque is measured in Newton-metre.

Dynamics of Rotational Motion about a Fi.question: A flywheel has a moment of inertia of 8 kg·m². To produce an angular acceleration of 6 rad/s², the required torque is:
Which factor does not affect the angular acceleration produced by a given torque?
Dynamics of Rotational Motion about a Fi.solution: Angular acceleration depends on τ and I, not on ω.

Dynamics of Rotational Motion about a Fi.question: Two wheels experience the same torque. Wheel A has twice the moment of inertia of Wheel B. Their angular accelerations satisfy:
Dynamics of Rotational Motion about a Fi.solution: α = τ/I. If I_A = 2I_B, then α_A = α_B/2.

Dynamics of Rotational Motion about a Fi.question: A constant torque acts on a rotating body. The graph of angular velocity versus time is:
options: B) Straight line with positive slope
Dynamics of Rotational Motion about a Fi.solution: A constant torque gives constant angular acceleration, so ω increases linearly with time.

Dynamics of Rotational Motion about a Fi.question: Which statement is correct?
options: A) Larger torque always means larger angular velocity.
C) Moment of inertia causes torque.
D) Torque and angular momentum have the same SI unit and are the same physical quantity.
Dynamics of Rotational Motion about a Fi.solution: Torque changes the rotational motion by producing angular acceleration.

Angular Momentum in Rotation about a Fix.question: A wheel has a moment of inertia of 8 kg·m² and rotates with an angular velocity of 5 rad/s. Its angular momentum is:
Angular Momentum in Rotation about a Fix.solution: L = Iω = 8×5 = 40 kg·m²/s

Angular Momentum in Rotation about a Fix.question: Assertion (A): In the absence of external torque, angular momentum remains conserved. Reason (R): External torque is equal to the rate of change of angular momentum.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation.
A is true, R is false.
A is false, R is true.
Angular Momentum in Rotation about a Fix.solution: τ = dL/dt. If τ = 0, L is constant.

Angular Momentum in Rotation about a Fix.question: A rotating disc has an angular momentum of 72 kg·m²/s and a moment of inertia of 9 kg·m². Its angular velocity is:
Angular Momentum in Rotation about a Fix.solution: ω = L/I = 72/9 = 8 rad/s

Angular Momentum in Rotation about a Fix.question: Which equation correctly relates torque and angular momentum?
Angular Momentum in Rotation about a Fix.solution: τ = dL/dt

Angular Momentum in Rotation about a Fix.question: A skater spinning with arms extended pulls her arms inward. Assuming no external torque acts, her:
Angular Momentum in Rotation about a Fix.solution: Angular momentum is conserved when no external torque acts.

Angular Momentum in Rotation about a Fix.question: A wheel initially has a moment of inertia of 10 kg·m² and angular velocity of 4 rad/s. Its moment of inertia decreases to 5 kg·m² without external torque. The new angular velocity is:
Angular Momentum in Rotation about a Fix.solution: L = I₁ω₁ = I₂ω₂ ⇒ 10×4 = 5×ω₂ ⇒ ω₂ = 8 rad/s

Angular Momentum in Rotation about a Fix.question: Angular momentum is a:
Angular Momentum in Rotation about a Fix.solution: Angular momentum is a vector quantity.

Angular Momentum in Rotation about a Fix.question: Which of the following has the same SI unit as angular momentum?
Angular Momentum in Rotation about a Fix.solution: Planck's constant has the same unit as angular momentum: kg·m²/s.

Angular Momentum in Rotation about a Fix.question: A constant external torque acts on a body. Its angular momentum:
Angular Momentum in Rotation about a Fix.solution: τ = dL/dt. Constant τ means L increases linearly with time.

Angular Momentum in Rotation about a Fix.question: A body rotates with constant angular velocity. Its angular momentum:
Angular Momentum in Rotation about a Fix.solution: L = Iω. If ω is constant, L is constant.

Angular Momentum in Rotation about a Fix.question: A flywheel has an angular momentum of 120 kg·m²/s. If its angular velocity is 15 rad/s, its moment of inertia is:
Which physical law explains why planets sweep out equal areas in equal intervals of time?
Angular Momentum in Rotation about a Fix.solution: Kepler's Second Law is based on conservation of angular momentum.

Angular Momentum in Rotation about a Fix.question: If the external torque on a system is zero, which quantity must remain constant?
Angular Momentum in Rotation about a Fix.solution: Angular momentum is conserved when external torque is zero.

Angular Momentum in Rotation about a Fix.question: A rotating body has twice the moment of inertia and half the angular velocity of another body. Compared to the second body, its angular momentum is:
Which statement is correct?
options: A) Angular momentum depends only on mass.
B) Angular momentum depends only on angular velocity.
C) Angular momentum depends on both moment of inertia and angular velocity.
D) Angular momentum is independent of the axis of rotation.
Angular Momentum in Rotation about a Fix.solution: L = Iω, so it depends on both I and ω.

Centre of Mass.question: A uniform rod of length 8 m has masses 2 kg, 3 kg, and 5 kg attached at distances 0 m, 3 m, and 8 m respectively from one end. The rod itself has a mass of 10 kg. The position of the centre of mass from the left end is:

Two particles of masses m and 3m are placed at the ends of a rod of length L. The rod is cut at the centre and replaced by a massless spring of negligible length. The position of the centre of mass of the system will:
options: A) Shift towards the lighter mass
B) Shift towards the heavier mass
Centre of Mass.solution: Centre of mass depends only on masses and their relative positions, not on how they are connected.

Centre of Mass.question: A uniform circular disc has a circular hole cut from it. The hole has radius R/2 and its centre is at a distance R/2 from the centre of the disc. The centre of mass shifts:
Centre of Mass.solution: Removing mass from one side shifts the centre of mass away from the removed mass.

Centre of Mass.question: Assertion (A): The centre of mass of an isolated system may accelerate even if internal forces are extremely large. Reason (R): Internal forces can produce acceleration of individual particles but cannot accelerate the centre of mass.
options: Both A and R are true, and R explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A.
A is false, R is true.
Centre of Mass.solution: Internal forces cannot accelerate the centre of mass. A is false, R is true.

Centre of Mass.question: Three particles each of mass m are placed at (0,0), (4,0), (0,6). The coordinates of the centre of mass are:
A system consists of four equal masses at the vertices of a square. One mass is suddenly removed. The centre of mass:
options: B) Shifts toward the removed corner
C) Shifts opposite the removed corner
Centre of Mass.solution: Removing a mass shifts the centre of mass away from the removed mass, i.e., opposite the removed corner.

Centre of Mass.question: A particle moves from (2,1) to (8,5) while another identical particle moves from (4,3) to (0,7). The displacement of the centre of mass is:
A body consists of two masses connected by a light rod. If the rod length is doubled while keeping masses fixed, the centre of mass:
options: B) Moves away from heavier mass
C) Changes depending upon mass ratio
D) Remains at the same fractional position along the rod
Centre of Mass.solution: The fractional position of centre of mass along the rod remains same as it depends on mass ratio.

Centre of Mass.question: The centre of mass of a system lies outside the material of the object in:
Centre of Mass.solution: For a hollow ring, the centre of mass is at the centre where there is no material.

Centre of Mass.question: A uniform rod is bent into an L-shape without stretching. Its centre of mass:
options: B) Depends on the new geometry
Centre of Mass.solution: Centre of mass depends on the geometry, which changes when the rod is bent.

Centre of Mass.question: A uniform rod of length L and mass M has a particle of mass M attached to one end. The system is placed along the x-axis. The centre of mass from the end carrying the particle is:
A square of side a has equal masses m at three of its corners. The fourth corner is empty. The distance of the centre of mass from the empty corner is:
Centre of Mass.solution: Taking empty corner as origin, x_cm = (0+a+a)/3 = 2a/3, y_cm = (0+0+a)/3 = a/3. Distance = √[(2a/3)² + (a/3)²] = (√5 a)/3

Centre of Mass.question: A uniform semicircular wire of radius R has its diameter along the x-axis. The y-coordinate of its centre of mass is:
Centre of Mass.solution: For a semicircular wire, y_cm = 2R/π

Centre of Mass.question: Two particles of masses m and 2m are located at coordinates (2,3) and (8,9) respectively. The coordinates of the centre of mass are:

A circular disc of radius R has a circular hole of radius R/3 cut from it. The centre of the hole is at a distance R/2 from the centre of the disc. The shift of the centre of mass from the original centre is:

Motion of Centre of Mass.question: A shell is fired at an angle of 45° with speed 40 m/s. At the highest point, it explodes into two equal fragments. One fragment comes to rest immediately after the explosion. Neglect air resistance. The horizontal speed of the second fragment immediately after the explosion is:
Motion of Centre of Mass.solution: At highest point, v_x = 40 cos45° = 20√2 m/s. Momentum conservation: 2m(20√2) = m(0) + m(v) ⇒ v = 40√2 m/s

Motion of Centre of Mass.question: Assertion (A): The centre of mass of a system can move even when every particle of the system is momentarily at rest. Reason (R): The centre of mass depends upon the distribution of mass as well as velocities of particles.
options: Both A and R are true, and R explains A.
Both true, but R doesn't explain A.
A is false, R is true.
Motion of Centre of Mass.solution: If every particle is at rest, the centre of mass must also be at rest. Both statements are false.

Motion of Centre of Mass.question: Two masses 2m, 3m move with velocities 4î, -2î respectively. Velocity of centre of mass is:
A bomb explodes into three fragments. External force is negligible. Which quantity remains unchanged immediately after explosion?
options: D) Speed of centre of mass
Motion of Centre of Mass.solution: Total momentum is conserved in absence of external force.

Motion of Centre of Mass.question: A person of mass 60 kg walks from one end to the other of a boat of mass 120 kg. Initially both are at rest. Boat length: 6 m. Boat displacement relative to water is:
Motion of Centre of Mass.solution: By conservation of centre of mass: 60×6 = (60+120)x ⇒ x = 360/180 = 2 m

Motion of Centre of Mass.question: A rocket moves in deep space. Fuel burns inside the rocket. Which quantity remains conserved for the rocket-fuel system?
Motion of Centre of Mass.solution: Total momentum of rocket-fuel system is conserved in absence of external forces.

Motion of Centre of Mass.question: Three equal masses move with velocities 2î, 3î, -5î. Velocity of centre of mass is:
A shell explodes into two unequal fragments. Ignoring external forces, the centre of mass:
options: C) Continues along the original trajectory
Motion of Centre of Mass.solution: Centre of mass continues along the original trajectory as no external force acts.

Motion of Centre of Mass.question: A man walks inside a freely moving railway coach. The centre of mass of the man-coach system:
Motion of Centre of Mass.solution: No external force acts on the system, so centre of mass moves with constant velocity.

Motion of Centre of Mass.question: If external force acting on a system is doubled while total mass becomes four times, acceleration of COM becomes:
Motion of Centre of Mass.solution: a = F/M. If F doubles and M becomes 4 times, a becomes 2/4 = 1/2 times.

Motion of Centre of Mass.question: Two masses move perpendicular to each other. Their momentum vectors are 3î, 4ĵ. Resultant momentum magnitude is:
A particle system experiences only internal forces. Acceleration of centre of mass is:
Motion of Centre of Mass.solution: Internal forces cannot accelerate the centre of mass.

Motion of Centre of Mass.question: The centre of mass of a system is moving with constant velocity. Which statement must be true?
Motion of Centre of Mass.solution: For constant velocity, acceleration is zero, so net external force must be zero.

Motion of Centre of Mass.question: A body breaks into four fragments due to an internal explosion. The velocity of the centre of mass immediately after explosion:
Motion of Centre of Mass.solution: Internal forces cannot change the velocity of the centre of mass.

Motion of Centre of Mass.question: Which statement is always true for an isolated system?
options: C) Centre of mass moves with constant velocity.
D) All particles move with constant velocity.
Motion of Centre of Mass.solution: For an isolated system, net external force is zero, so centre of mass moves with constant velocity.

Linear Momentum of a System of Particles.question: Two particles of masses 2 kg and 3 kg move along the x-axis with velocities 4 m/s and -2 m/s, respectively. The total linear momentum of the system is:
Assertion (A): In an isolated system, the total linear momentum remains constant. Reason (R): Internal forces always occur in equal and opposite pairs.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A.
A is true, R is false.
A is false, R is true.
Linear Momentum of a System of Particles.solution: Internal forces cancel out, so external forces are required to change total momentum.

Linear Momentum of a System of Particles.question: A shell of mass 10 kg moving at 20 m/s explodes into two fragments of masses 4 kg and 6 kg. If the 4 kg fragment moves at 35 m/s in the original direction, the velocity of the 6 kg fragment is:
A force acts on a system of particles. The rate of change of total linear momentum equals:
Two identical balls move with equal speeds in opposite directions. The total momentum of the system is:
options: B) Equal to momentum of one ball
Linear Momentum of a System of Particles.solution: Momentum vectors cancel, so total momentum is zero.

Linear Momentum of a System of Particles.question: A body of mass 4 kg moving at 8 m/s collides head-on with a body of mass 2 kg moving at -4 m/s. The total momentum before collision is:
Which of the following is always conserved during any collision in an isolated system?
Linear Momentum of a System of Particles.solution: Linear momentum is always conserved in collisions in an isolated system.

Linear Momentum of a System of Particles.question: A rocket ejects fuel backward in space. The forward motion of the rocket is explained by:
Linear Momentum of a System of Particles.solution: Rocket propulsion is based on conservation of linear momentum.

Linear Momentum of a System of Particles.question: Three particles of masses 1 kg, 2 kg, and 3 kg move with velocities 2 m/s, 3 m/s, and -4 m/s, respectively, along the x-axis. The total momentum is:
A body explodes into four fragments. The vector sum of the momenta of all fragments is:
options: A) Zero only if initially at rest
B) Always equal to the initial momentum
Linear Momentum of a System of Particles.solution: By conservation of momentum, total momentum equals initial momentum.

Linear Momentum of a System of Particles.question: Two particles have equal momentum. If the mass of one particle is doubled, its speed compared to the other is:
Linear Momentum of a System of Particles.solution: p = mv. If p is constant and m doubles, v becomes half.

Linear Momentum of a System of Particles.question: A constant external force acts on a system for 5 s, producing an impulse of 40 N·s. The change in total momentum is:
Linear Momentum of a System of Particles.solution: Impulse = Change in momentum = 40 N·s = 40 kg·m/s

Linear Momentum of a System of Particles.question: Two particles move at right angles with momenta 6 kg·m/s and 8 kg·m/s. The magnitude of the resultant momentum is:
A system has zero total momentum. Which statement is necessarily true?
options: A) Every particle is at rest.
B) Centre of mass is at rest or moves with constant velocity if initially moving.
