Linear Momentum of a System of Particles.solution: Zero total momentum means centre of mass velocity is zero (or constant if initially moving).

Linear Momentum of a System of Particles.question: Two bodies of masses m and 2m move with velocities 6 m/s and v, respectively. If the total momentum of the system is zero, the value of v is:

Vector Product (Cross Product) of Two Ve.question: The magnitude of the vector product of two vectors A and B is:
Vector Product (Cross Product) of Two Ve.solution: |A×B| = AB sinθ

Vector Product (Cross Product) of Two Ve.question: Assertion (A): The cross product of two parallel vectors is zero. Reason (R): The angle between parallel vectors is either 0° or 180°.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both true, but R is not the correct explanation.
A is true, R is false.
A is false, R is true.
Vector Product (Cross Product) of Two Ve.solution: |A×B| = AB sinθ. For parallel vectors, sinθ = 0, so cross product is zero.

Vector Product (Cross Product) of Two Ve.question: Two vectors each of magnitude 5 make an angle of 30°. The magnitude of their cross product is:
The direction of A⃗×B⃗ is determined by:
Vector Product (Cross Product) of Two Ve.solution: Both Right-Hand Thumb Rule and Right-Hand Screw Rule give the direction.

Vector Product (Cross Product) of Two Ve.question: If A⃗ = 3î and B⃗ = 4ĵ, then A⃗×B⃗ is:
The value of ĵ×î is:
The cross product of any vector with itself is:
If A⃗×B⃗ = 0⃗, then:
options: B) Vectors are parallel or one vector is zero.
C) Both vectors have equal magnitude.
D) Both vectors are unit vectors.
Vector Product (Cross Product) of Two Ve.solution: A×B = 0 when vectors are parallel, anti-parallel, or one is zero.

Vector Product (Cross Product) of Two Ve.question: The area of the parallelogram formed by vectors A⃗, B⃗ is:
Vector Product (Cross Product) of Two Ve.solution: Area of parallelogram = |A×B|

Vector Product (Cross Product) of Two Ve.question: The area of the triangle formed by vectors A⃗, B⃗ is:
Vector Product (Cross Product) of Two Ve.solution: Area of triangle = 1/2|A×B|

Vector Product (Cross Product) of Two Ve.question: If A⃗ = 2î+ĵ and B⃗ = î+3ĵ, then A⃗×B⃗ is:
Which of the following quantities is obtained using a vector product?
Vector Product (Cross Product) of Two Ve.solution: Torque = r×F, which is a vector product.

Vector Product (Cross Product) of Two Ve.question: If two vectors are perpendicular, the magnitude of their cross product is:
Vector Product (Cross Product) of Two Ve.solution: For perpendicular vectors, θ = 90°, so |A×B| = AB sin90° = AB

Vector Product (Cross Product) of Two Ve.question: Which of the following is NOT true?
Vector Product (Cross Product) of Two Ve.solution: Cross product is anti-commutative, so A×B = -B×A, not B×A.

Vector Product (Cross Product) of Two Ve.question: Two vectors have magnitudes 8 and 15. Their cross product has magnitude 120. The angle between them is:

Angular Velocity and its Relation with L.question: A wheel of radius 0.5 m rotates with an angular velocity of 20 rad/s. The linear speed of a point on its rim is:
Assertion (A): All particles of a rigid body rotating about a fixed axis have the same angular velocity. Reason (R): Angular velocity is independent of the distance from the axis.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation.
A is true, R is false.
A is false, R is true.
Angular Velocity and its Relation with L.solution: Angular velocity is same for all points in a rigid body.

Angular Velocity and its Relation with L.question: Two particles are located at distances R and 3R from the axis of rotation. If the body rotates with angular velocity ω, the ratio of their linear speeds is:
Angular Velocity and its Relation with L.solution: v = rω, so v₁:v₂ = R:3R = 1:3

Angular Velocity and its Relation with L.question: A wheel rotates at 300 rpm. Its angular velocity is:
A point on the rim of a rotating disc has speed 12 m/s. If the radius of the disc is doubled while angular velocity remains constant, the new linear speed becomes:
Angular Velocity and its Relation with L.solution: v = rω. If r doubles, v doubles to 24 m/s.

Angular Velocity and its Relation with L.question: A rotating fan has angular velocity 15 rad/s. A point is 0.4 m from the centre. Its centripetal acceleration is:
The relation between angular velocity and frequency is:
Angular Velocity and its Relation with L.solution: ω = 2πf

Angular Velocity and its Relation with L.question: Two wheels rotate with the same angular velocity. Their radii are in the ratio 2 : 5. The ratio of linear speeds at their rims is:
Angular Velocity and its Relation with L.solution: v = rω. With same ω, v ∝ r, so ratio = 2:5

Angular Velocity and its Relation with L.question: A car tyre of radius 0.35 m rolls without slipping with speed 14 m/s. Its angular velocity is:
A point moves in a circle of radius 2 m with angular velocity 6 rad/s. The magnitude of its velocity is:
If the angular velocity of a rotating body becomes three times, the centripetal acceleration of a point on its rim becomes:
Angular Velocity and its Relation with L.solution: a_c = rω². If ω triples, a_c becomes 9 times.

Angular Velocity and its Relation with L.question: Which quantity remains the same for every point of a rigid body rotating about a fixed axis?
Angular Velocity and its Relation with L.solution: All points have the same angular velocity.

Angular Velocity and its Relation with L.question: A rotating disc has radius 0.8 m and rotates with angular speed 5 rad/s. The speed of a point 0.2 m from the centre is:
A wheel rotates uniformly. Which graph correctly represents the relation between linear speed v and distance r from the centre?
options: B) Straight line passing through origin
Angular Velocity and its Relation with L.solution: v = rω. For constant ω, v ∝ r, so graph is a straight line through origin.

Angular Velocity and its Relation with L.question: A rigid body rotates about a fixed axis with angular velocity ω. Which statement is correct?
options: A) Every point has the same linear velocity.
B) Every point has the same angular velocity but different linear velocities.
C) Linear velocity is independent of radius.
D) Linear velocity decreases with radius.
Angular Velocity and its Relation with L.solution: All points have same ω but different v = rω.

Torque and Angular Momentum.question: A force of 20 N acts perpendicular to a rod of length 0.5 m pivoted at one end. The torque about the pivot is:
Assertion (A): If the net external torque on a system is zero, its angular momentum remains constant. Reason (R): Torque is equal to the time rate of change of angular momentum.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation.
A is true, R is false.
A is false, R is true.
Torque and Angular Momentum.solution: τ = dL/dt. If τ = 0, L is constant.

Torque and Angular Momentum.question: A disc has a moment of inertia of 5 kg·m² and rotates at 12 rad/s. Its angular momentum is:
Torque and Angular Momentum.solution: L = Iω = 5×12 = 60 kg·m²/s

Torque and Angular Momentum.question: A particle is moving in a circle of radius 4 m with momentum 15 kg·m/s. Its angular momentum about the centre is:
Torque and Angular Momentum.solution: L = r×p = 4×15 = 60 kg·m²/s

Torque and Angular Momentum.question: If both the force and perpendicular distance from the axis are doubled, the torque becomes:
Torque and Angular Momentum.solution: τ = rF. If r doubles and F doubles, τ becomes 4 times.

Torque and Angular Momentum.question: A flywheel rotates freely without any external torque. Its angular momentum:
Torque and Angular Momentum.solution: No external torque means angular momentum is conserved.

Torque and Angular Momentum.question: Two identical discs rotate with angular speeds ω and 2ω. Their angular momenta are in the ratio:
Torque and Angular Momentum.solution: L = Iω. For identical discs, I is same, so L ∝ ω. Ratio = 1:2

Torque and Angular Momentum.question: A skater reduces her moment of inertia to one-third of its initial value while no external torque acts. Her angular speed becomes:
Torque and Angular Momentum.solution: L = Iω constant. If I becomes I/3, ω becomes 3ω.

Torque and Angular Momentum.question: The SI unit of angular momentum is:
Torque and Angular Momentum.solution: 1 kg·m²/s = 1 J·s

Torque and Angular Momentum.question: A body experiences a constant torque of 8 N·m for 5 s. The change in angular momentum is:
Torque and Angular Momentum.solution: ΔL = τ×t = 8×5 = 40 kg·m²/s

Torque and Angular Momentum.question: A force acts through the axis of rotation. The torque produced is:
Torque and Angular Momentum.solution: τ = rF sinθ. If force acts through axis, r = 0, so τ = 0.

Torque and Angular Momentum.question: Which of the following is not a vector quantity?
Torque and Angular Momentum.solution: Moment of inertia is a scalar quantity.

Torque and Angular Momentum.question: A body rotating about a fixed axis has angular momentum L. If its moment of inertia is doubled without any external torque, the new angular velocity becomes:
Torque and Angular Momentum.solution: L = Iω constant. If I doubles, ω becomes half.

Torque and Angular Momentum.question: A force F⃗ = 4ĵ acts at the point r⃗ = 3î. The torque is:
A rotating system is subjected to zero external torque. Which of the following may still change?
Torque and Angular Momentum.solution: If moment of inertia changes (e.g., skater pulling in arms), angular velocity changes while angular momentum remains constant.

Equilibrium of a Rigid Body.question: A rigid body is in complete equilibrium if:
options: A) Net force is zero only
B) Net torque is zero only
C) Both net force and net torque are zero
Equilibrium of a Rigid Body.solution: Complete equilibrium requires both ΣF = 0 and Στ = 0.

Equilibrium of a Rigid Body.question: Assertion (A): A body may have zero net force but still rotate. Reason (R): Zero net force does not necessarily imply zero net torque.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both true, but R is not the correct explanation.
A is true, R is false.
A is false, R is true.
Equilibrium of a Rigid Body.solution: A couple produces zero net force but non-zero torque.

Equilibrium of a Rigid Body.question: A uniform rod of length 4 m and weight 120 N is supported at its centre. A load of 60 N is placed 1 m from the centre. To maintain equilibrium, another load should be placed:
options: A) 0.5 m on the opposite side
B) 1 m on the opposite side
C) 2 m on the opposite side
D) 4 m on the opposite side
Equilibrium of a Rigid Body.solution: 60×1 = F×d. For equilibrium with 60 N load, F must be 60 N at d = 1 m.

Equilibrium of a Rigid Body.question: A couple consists of:
options: A) Two equal parallel forces acting in the same direction
C) Two equal and opposite parallel forces separated by a distance
Equilibrium of a Rigid Body.solution: A couple is two equal and opposite parallel forces separated by a distance.

Equilibrium of a Rigid Body.question: The SI unit of the moment of a couple is:
Equilibrium of a Rigid Body.solution: Moment of couple = Force × distance, unit is N·m.

Equilibrium of a Rigid Body.question: A body is acted upon by three coplanar forces. For equilibrium, these forces must:
options: C) Form a closed triangle when represented as vectors
Equilibrium of a Rigid Body.solution: For equilibrium, vector sum of forces must be zero, forming a closed triangle.

Equilibrium of a Rigid Body.question: A ladder rests against a smooth wall and rough floor. The friction acts:
options: C) At both wall and floor
Equilibrium of a Rigid Body.solution: Smooth wall means no friction; friction acts only at the rough floor.

Equilibrium of a Rigid Body.question: If equal clockwise and anticlockwise torques act simultaneously on a body, the body:
Equilibrium of a Rigid Body.solution: Equal and opposite torques cancel, so net torque is zero.

Equilibrium of a Rigid Body.question: A beam of negligible weight carries loads 20 N and 40 N at distances 2 m and 1 m from a pivot on opposite sides. The beam is:
Equilibrium of a Rigid Body.solution: 20×2 = 40×1 = 40 N·m. Torques balance, so beam is in equilibrium.

Equilibrium of a Rigid Body.question: A rigid body is under the action of several forces. Its translational equilibrium depends upon:
Equilibrium of a Rigid Body.solution: Translational equilibrium requires vector sum of forces to be zero.

Equilibrium of a Rigid Body.question: Which of the following quantities is not required to determine torque?
options: C) Angle between force and position vector
Equilibrium of a Rigid Body.solution: Torque depends on force, distance, and angle, not on mass.

Equilibrium of a Rigid Body.question: A uniform beam is balanced horizontally by a support at its centre. If an additional load is placed exactly at the support point, then:
Equilibrium of a Rigid Body.solution: Load at support point produces no torque, so equilibrium is maintained.

Equilibrium of a Rigid Body.question: A body is in rotational equilibrium but not in translational equilibrium. Which statement is true?
Equilibrium of a Rigid Body.solution: Rotational equilibrium means net torque is zero, even if net force is not zero.

Equilibrium of a Rigid Body.question: The centre of gravity and centre of mass of a body coincide when:
Equilibrium of a Rigid Body.solution: Centre of gravity equals centre of mass only when gravitational field is uniform.

Equilibrium of a Rigid Body.question: A uniform rod is hinged at one end and held horizontally by a vertical string at the other end. If the string breaks instantly, the initial angular acceleration of the rod about the hinge is:
Equilibrium of a Rigid Body.solution: τ = Iα ⇒ Mg(L/2) = (ML²/3)α ⇒ α = 3g/2L

Moment of Inertia.question: A solid disc of mass 4 kg and radius 0.5 m rotates about its central axis. Its moment of inertia is:
Assertion (A): The moment of inertia of a body depends on the axis of rotation. Reason (R): Moment of inertia depends on the distribution of mass about the axis.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both true, but R is not the correct explanation.
A is true, R is false.
A is false, R is true.
Moment of Inertia.solution: Different axes mean different mass distribution relative to axis.

Moment of Inertia.question: A ring and a solid disc have the same mass and radius. The ratio of their moments of inertia about the central axis is:
Moment of Inertia.solution: I_ring = MR², I_disc = 1/2 MR². Ratio = 2:1

Moment of Inertia.question: A thin rod of length L rotates about its centre. Its moment of inertia is:
Moment of Inertia.solution: I_rod, centre = ML²/12

Moment of Inertia.question: Using the Parallel Axis Theorem, I = I_cm + Md². If the axis passes through the centre of mass, d =
Moment of Inertia.solution: When axis passes through centre of mass, d = 0.

Moment of Inertia.question: A solid sphere has moment of inertia:
Moment of Inertia.solution: I_sphere = 2/5 MR²

Moment of Inertia.question: If the mass of a body is doubled while its radius remains unchanged, its moment of inertia becomes:
Moment of Inertia.solution: I ∝ M. If M doubles, I doubles.

Moment of Inertia.question: A body has a radius of gyration k. Its moment of inertia is:
Moment of Inertia.solution: I = Mk²

Moment of Inertia.question: A thin ring has mass 2 kg and radius 0.4 m. Its moment of inertia is:
The Radius of Gyration is:
options: A) The actual radius of the body
B) The distance at which the whole mass may be assumed concentrated without changing the moment of inertia
C) Radius of the centre of mass
Moment of Inertia.solution: Radius of gyration is the effective distance where all mass can be concentrated.

Moment of Inertia.question: A rod rotates about one end. Its moment of inertia is:
Moment of Inertia.solution: I_rod, end = ML²/3

Moment of Inertia.question: Which theorem is used to calculate the moment of inertia about an axis parallel to the centre of mass axis?
Moment of Inertia.solution: Parallel Axis Theorem: I = I_cm + Md²

Moment of Inertia.question: The Perpendicular Axis Theorem is applicable only for:
Moment of Inertia.solution: Perpendicular Axis Theorem applies to plane laminae (2D objects).

Moment of Inertia.question: A body has a moment of inertia of 8 kg·m² about its centre of mass. Its mass is 2 kg. The axis is shifted by 3 m. The new moment of inertia is:
Moment of Inertia.solution: I = I_cm + Md² = 8 + 2×9 = 26 kg·m²

Moment of Inertia.question: Two bodies have the same mass but different distributions of mass about the axis. Which statement is correct?
options: A) Their moments of inertia are always equal.
B) The body with mass farther from the axis has a larger moment of inertia.
C) Moment of inertia depends only on mass.
D) Moment of inertia is independent of shape.
Moment of Inertia.solution: I = ∑mr². Mass farther from axis gives larger I.

Kinematics of Rotational Motion about a.question: A wheel starts from rest and rotates with a constant angular acceleration of 4 rad/s². Its angular velocity after 5 s is:

Assertion (A): The rotational equations of motion are analogous to linear equations of motion. Reason (R): Angular displacement, angular velocity and angular acceleration correspond to displacement, velocity and acceleration respectively.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation.
A is true, R is false.
A is false, R is true.
Kinematics of Rotational Motion about a.solution: The analogy between linear and rotational motion is well-established.

A wheel rotating at 30 rad/s is uniformly brought to rest in 6 s. Its angular acceleration is:
A wheel rotates through 80 rad while slowing uniformly from 20 rad/s to 12 rad/s. Its angular acceleration is:
The angular displacement of a body rotating with constant angular velocity 10 rad/s in 8 s is:
Which equation is NOT a rotational equation of motion?
Kinematics of Rotational Motion about a.solution: ω = αθ is not a standard rotational equation of motion.

Dynamics of Rotational Motion about a Fi.question: A solid disc of moment of inertia 4 kg·m² is acted upon by a constant torque of 20 N·m. The angular acceleration produced is:
Dynamics of Rotational Motion about a Fi.solution: α = τ/I = 20/4 = 5 rad/s²

Dynamics of Rotational Motion about a Fi.question: Assertion (A): A larger moment of inertia produces a smaller angular acceleration for the same applied torque. Reason (R): Angular acceleration is inversely proportional to moment of inertia.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation.
A is true, R is false.
A is false, R is true.
Dynamics of Rotational Motion about a Fi.solution: α = τ/I. For constant τ, α ∝ 1/I.

Dynamics of Rotational Motion about a Fi.question: A flywheel has a moment of inertia of 10 kg·m². A torque of 50 N·m acts on it for 4 s. The final angular velocity if initially at rest is:
Dynamics of Rotational Motion about a Fi.solution: α = 50/10 = 5 rad/s², ω = αt = 5×4 = 20 rad/s

Dynamics of Rotational Motion about a Fi.question: A torque of 15 N·m acts on a wheel producing an angular acceleration of 3 rad/s². The moment of inertia is:
Dynamics of Rotational Motion about a Fi.solution: I = τ/α = 15/3 = 5 kg·m²

Dynamics of Rotational Motion about a Fi.question: Rotational kinetic energy of a body is:
Dynamics of Rotational Motion about a Fi.solution: K_rot = 1/2 Iω²

Dynamics of Rotational Motion about a Fi.question: A disc rotates with angular velocity 8 rad/s. Its moment of inertia is 5 kg·m². Its rotational kinetic energy is:
The rotational analogue of force is:
Dynamics of Rotational Motion about a Fi.solution: Torque is the rotational analogue of force.

Dynamics of Rotational Motion about a Fi.question: The rotational analogue of mass is:
Dynamics of Rotational Motion about a Fi.solution: Moment of inertia is the rotational analogue of mass.

Dynamics of Rotational Motion about a Fi.question: A wheel rotating at 20 rad/s has rotational kinetic energy 800 J. Its moment of inertia is:
If the applied torque is doubled while the moment of inertia remains constant, angular acceleration becomes:
Dynamics of Rotational Motion about a Fi.solution: α = τ/I. If τ doubles, α doubles.

Dynamics of Rotational Motion about a Fi.question: A motor delivers constant torque to a rotating shaft. The angular acceleration will remain constant only if:
options: B) Moment of inertia remains constant
Dynamics of Rotational Motion about a Fi.solution: α = τ/I. For constant α with constant τ, I must remain constant.

Dynamics of Rotational Motion about a Fi.question: A body has rotational kinetic energy 450 J and moment of inertia 2 kg·m². Its angular velocity is:
The work done by a constant torque is:
Dynamics of Rotational Motion about a Fi.solution: W = τθ

Dynamics of Rotational Motion about a Fi.question: A torque of 8 N·m rotates a wheel through 12 rad. The work done is:
A rotating body has constant rotational kinetic energy. Which of the following must also remain constant?
Dynamics of Rotational Motion about a Fi.solution: K = 1/2 Iω² constant means Iω² is constant.

Angular Momentum in Case of Rotation abo.question: A solid cylinder of moment of inertia 8 kg·m² rotates with an angular velocity of 5 rad/s. Its angular momentum is:
Assertion (A): If no external torque acts on a rotating body, its angular momentum remains constant. Reason (R): Angular momentum is conserved only when rotational kinetic energy remains constant.
options: Both A and R are true, and R explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A.
A is true, R is false.
A is false, R is true.
Angular Momentum in Case of Rotation abo.solution: A is true, but R is false. Angular momentum can be conserved even when KE changes (e.g., skater pulling arms).

Angular Momentum in Case of Rotation abo.question: A skater rotates with angular speed 3 rad/s. She pulls her arms inward and her moment of inertia becomes one-third of the original value. Her new angular speed is:
A wheel has moment of inertia 2 kg·m² and angular momentum 50 kg·m²/s. Its angular velocity is:
The SI unit of angular momentum is:
A body rotates with constant angular velocity. Its angular momentum remains constant provided:
options: B) Moment of inertia remains constant
Angular Momentum in Case of Rotation abo.solution: L = Iω. For constant ω, L is constant if I is constant.

Angular Momentum in Case of Rotation abo.question: The direction of angular momentum is determined by:
Angular Momentum in Case of Rotation abo.solution: Right-Hand Thumb Rule gives the direction of angular momentum.

Angular Momentum in Case of Rotation abo.question: A body rotates with angular velocity 10 rad/s. If its moment of inertia doubles due to redistribution of mass and no external torque acts, the new angular velocity becomes:
Angular Momentum in Case of Rotation abo.solution: L = Iω constant. If I doubles, ω becomes half: 10/2 = 5 rad/s.

Angular Momentum in Case of Rotation abo.question: A particle of mass 3 kg moves in a circle of radius 4 m with speed 5 m/s. Its angular momentum about the centre is:
The rotational analogue of linear momentum is:
Angular Momentum in Case of Rotation abo.solution: Angular momentum is the rotational analogue of linear momentum.

Angular Momentum in Case of Rotation abo.question: A rotating disc has angular momentum 80 kg·m²/s. If an external torque of 20 N·m acts in the opposite direction for 2 s, the final angular momentum is:
Angular momentum of a rigid body rotating about a fixed axis depends on:
options: C) Moment of inertia and angular velocity
Angular Momentum in Case of Rotation abo.solution: L = Iω, so depends on both I and ω.

Angular Momentum in Case of Rotation abo.question: A flywheel rotates freely in space. Which quantity is conserved?
Angular Momentum in Case of Rotation abo.solution: No external torque means angular momentum is conserved.

Angular Momentum in Case of Rotation abo.question: A child sitting on a rotating platform stretches out both arms. Ignoring friction, the platform's angular momentum:
Angular Momentum in Case of Rotation abo.solution: No external torque acts, so angular momentum remains constant.

Angular Momentum in Case of Rotation abo.question: A satellite moving in a circular orbit around Earth experiences no external torque about Earth's centre. Which quantity remains constant?
options: C) Angular momentum about Earth's centre
Angular Momentum in Case of Rotation abo.solution: No external torque means angular momentum is conserved.
